name: SEO
blurb: Get pages crawled, indexed and chosen — by Google, Bing and AI answer engines. Audits, content, schema, local, links.
searches: Google Search Central update new documentation this week
Google core update ranking volatility analysis
AI Overviews ChatGPT Perplexity citation study new data
Core Web Vitals INP new guidance or tooling
agent skill SEO audit Claude new release

tests.prompt: Our blog's organic clicks fell 35% over the last 4 weeks while impressions stayed flat. Here is a Search Console export (query, page, clicks, impressions, position for both periods). Tell me what happened and what to do first.
tests.good: Notices flat impressions plus falling clicks points to CTR loss (SERP features or AI Overviews), not a ranking loss; segments by page and query; compares CTR to expected by position; separates observations from hypotheses; gives 1-3 ranked actions each with a verification check and re-measure dates; promises no recovery.

tests.prompt: Plan 200 '[integration] + our product' pages for our SaaS. We have a list of integration names and logos. Give me the template, the rollout plan and what would make you stop.
tests.good: Requires per-integration data beyond the name (setup steps, use cases, fields synced) and a unique-content threshold; uses subfolder URLs, hub-and-spoke links, its own sitemap; launches 10-20 first and checks the indexed rate after 4-8 weeks before scaling; names the swap test or doorway risk and when to noindex.

tests.prompt: Check whether our docs site is ready for AI search. robots.txt blocks GPTBot and ClaudeBot, pages are a client-side React app, and we have FAQPage schema on every page. What should change?
tests.good: Separates training bots from AI search and user-fetch bots (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-User) and checks CDN rules; flags CSR as the main problem and recommends SSR or SSG; says FAQ rich results are retired and FAQ schema is not an AI boost; suggests answer-first sections, optional llms.txt for docs, and a measured prompt set run 3-5 times.

tests.prompt: Organic clicks to our Next.js marketing site fell 30% after we moved the blog from /blog to /resources in August. Here's the Search Console export for both periods. Find what broke, fix it in the code, and refresh the three posts that lost the most clicks.
tests.good: States a short plan first: diagnosis here (audit.md, technical.md: redirects, canonicals, sitemaps and internal links for the moved URLs), code fixes through website-building (nextjs-react.md: single-hop 301s, canonicals and metadata in the server HTML), rewrites through content-creation (long-form-articles.md) after keywords-content.md sets each post's query cluster and SERP intent. Compares equal complete windows; keeps observations apart from causes; every finding has an evidence URL and date; fixes templates rather than single pages; sets 7, 14, 28 and 56-day re-measures; promises no recovery; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I have Screaming Frog SEO Spider on my Mac with a paid licence and a site of about 8,000 URLs. I want a crawl that runs from the terminal every Monday morning without opening the app, checks response codes, canonicals and noindex, and pulls in Search Console clicks so I can see which broken or non-indexable pages actually get traffic. Tell me the exact command and setup, what to export, and how to read the result.
tests.good: Uses the Screaming Frog command line in headless mode with real flags (crawl, headless, output folder, a saved config file made in the GUI, export-tabs and bulk-export choices, save-crawl) and does not invent options. Explains that the Search Console connection must be authorised once in the app and then referenced from the command and the saved configuration. Exports a small set of tabs (internal all, response codes with 4xx and 5xx, canonicals, directives noindex) rather than everything, and joins clicks to URLs to rank problems by traffic, noting that Search Console performance data is delayed (newest data can be preliminary) and incomplete (rare or anonymised queries are omitted and only top rows are stored); Google doesn't describe it as sampled. Still a Measured source with a date range.. Notes the licence is needed above 500 URLs, and that JavaScript rendering, crawl speed and respecting robots.txt affect an 8,000-URL crawl. Asks the owner before installing any scheduled job and shows the launchd or cron entry plus how to remove it, keeping credentials out of the script. Treats findings as observations with a failure check, and compares each run with the previous crawl instead of promising a ranking gain.

tools.name: Google Search Console
tools.why: Second most used SEO tool (49% of companies) in the Blogging Wizard 2026 roundup, and the first-party source for clicks, queries and indexing; its API has Search Analytics, URL Inspection, Sitemaps and Sites.

tools.name: Google Analytics 4
tools.why: Most commonly used SEO-adjacent tool (72% of companies) in the Blogging Wizard 2026 roundup; needed to tie organic landing pages to conversions and AI referrals. Google ships an official read-only MCP server.

tools.name: Semrush
tools.why: Most-used vendor in SEO software by Ramp's March 2026 data and in over 35% of Fortune 500 firms; official Claude connector and Apache-2.0 skills repo from Semrush itself.

tools.name: Ahrefs
tools.why: Used by 82% of surveyed link builders (Blogging Wizard 2026) and runs the most active SEO crawler after Googlebot (Cloudflare); official hosted MCP on Lite plans and up, billed in API units.

tools.name: Screaming Frog SEO Spider
tools.why: Named with Sitebulb as the two most widely used technical SEO crawlers in 2026 round-ups; version 24 added an official MCP server and it has had a headless command-line mode for years.

tools.name: PageSpeed Insights, CrUX and Lighthouse
tools.why: Google's own Core Web Vitals sources: the PSI v5 API returns Lighthouse lab data plus field data, Google is moving field data to the CrUX API, and Lighthouse (30k stars) is the CLI and CI standard.

tools.name: Yoast SEO and Rank Math (WordPress)
tools.why: Yoast has over 10 million active installs and Rank Math over 4 million (2026 comparisons), so most WordPress SEO work means setting titles, schema, redirects and sitemaps through one of them; Yoast documents a REST and Schema API.

tools.name: Google Keyword Planner
tools.why: Third most used SEO tool (36% of companies) in the Blogging Wizard 2026 roundup; the API gives keyword ideas and historical metrics but needs a developer token and Google Ads account, with tight rate limits.

tools.name: Bing Webmaster Tools and IndexNow
tools.why: Free Bing index, query and link data plus the URL submission API; matters more now that Copilot and several AI answer engines draw on the Bing index.

tools.name: Surfer
tools.why: The standard content-scoring and brief tool in 2026 round-ups; launched an official MCP (beta, August 2026) exposing Content Editor, AI Tracker and recommendations on its paid plans.

tools.name: Sitebulb
tools.why: One of the two most used technical crawlers with Screaming Frog; now has a hosted read-only MCP for both Cloud and Desktop audits (15 tools).

tools.name: DataForSEO
tools.why: Pay-per-call SERP, keyword, backlink, on-page and AI-visibility API behind many SEO tools; official MCP server (remote and npx) from the vendor.

tools.name: SE Ranking
tools.why: Mid-market all-in-one platform with an official hosted MCP (160+ tools incl. audits, backlinks and AI visibility), noted as the most complete official SEO MCP in 2026 round-ups.

tools.name: Moz Pro and Moz API
tools.why: Source of Domain Authority; the Links API has a free tier used as a low-cost backlink source. No official MCP server as of August 2026 (round-up reports). Docs page could not be fetched from this environment.

tools.name: Google Trends API
tools.why: Free attention and seasonality signal, now with an alpha official API (5 years of data, many terms per request); alpha access is by application.

tools.name: Google Business Profile
tools.why: The default and highest-weight tool for local SEO: Whitespark's 2026 local ranking factors put GBP signals at about 32% of local-pack weight, and every 2026 local SEO tool round-up (BrightLocal, Local Falcon, Whitespark) is built around managing it; Business Profile APIs cover locations, posts, reviews and performance for verified owners.

tools.name: Rich Results Test and Schema Markup Validator
tools.why: Google's own docs name the Rich Results Test as the way to validate structured data during development (with the Search Console rich result reports after deploy), and the router's 'Done means' requires schema to validate in it, so it is the default tool for the schema job; no API.

tools.name: BrightLocal
tools.why: Called the best overall local SEO platform for agencies in 2026 local-tool round-ups (rank and map tracking, citation audits and building, reviews, white-label reports); ships an official MCP (BrightLocal Anywhere, Grow plan plus Labs beta) and a REST API.

tools.name: Local Falcon
tools.why: Named the specialist Google Maps geo-grid rank tracker in 2026 local SEO round-ups and the source of the geo-grid scans local.md recommends; official remote MCP (MIT, OAuth or API key) with scan, campaign, GBP-monitoring and AI-visibility tools.

tools.name: Profound
tools.why: The enterprise leader in AI search visibility tracking in 2026 comparisons (Frase, Zapier and Rankability lists; popular with Fortune 100 brands), and AI search is a core job of this craft with no tracker in the list; official hosted MCP with visibility, citation, sentiment and shopping reports.

tools.name: Conductor
tools.why: One of the four enterprise SEO/AEO platforms every 2026 enterprise round-up compares (with BrightEdge, Botify, seoClarity), and it is in Claude's connector directory with an official MCP exposing keyword rankings, AI citations and competitive share.

tools.name: BrightEdge
tools.why: Ranked the all-in-one enterprise SEO leader for Fortune 500 teams in 2026 enterprise round-ups; read-only official MCP (OAuth with BrightEdge login) for rankings, share of voice, GSC data and AI visibility.

tools.name: Botify
tools.why: The enterprise technical-SEO crawler and log-analysis platform named best for large ecommerce and media sites in 2026 enterprise round-ups; official MCP and agents API (crawl, logs, GSC, SQL over tables) and an official Apache-2.0 skills plugin.
